column3: “Call out on it” is rendered “cry against it.”
“From before the LORD” is rendered “from the presence of the LORD”; “its fare” is rendered “the fare.”
“Threw” is rendered “hurled”; “the ship thought to be broken” is rendered “the ship was about to break up.”
“Vessels” is rendered “cargo,” and “innermost parts” “the hold”; “gone down” is rendered “gone below.”
“The chief of the sailors” is rendered “the captain,” and “give thought” “be concerned”; “what is to you, sleeping?” is rendered “How is it that you are sleeping?”
“Neighbor” is rendered “mate,” and “the evil” “calamity”; NASB supplies “has struck.”
“Feared a great fear” is rendered “became extremely frightened,” and “What is this you have done?” “How could you do this?”
“Going and storming” is rendered “becoming increasingly stormy.”
“By which to me” is rendered “on account of me.”
“Rowed” is rendered “rowed desperately,” adding “desperately”; “dry land” is rendered “land.”
“We beg you” is rendered “We earnestly pray”; “by the life of” is rendered “on account of this man’s life.”
“Stopped from its storming” is rendered “stopped its raging.”
“Feared a great fear” is rendered “feared … greatly”; “sacrificed a sacrifice” is rendered “offered a sacrifice.”
